findings.summary: Reuse javascriptModuleUrl for Babylon hierarchy execution and shared AST assignment/update predicates for animation writer discovery.
Remove the unused animation master clock and node map; retain the source binding plan only during resource hydration.
Remove three unused glTF loader options and their call arguments while retaining the independently reached animation APIs.
Share the node-particle metadata tuple across the six value kinds that use it.
Reuse source material and light snapshots after pointer publication and retain only observed flags that have readers.
Use identity sets for source material-output removal and replacement membership.
Index weighted animation targets by node-array identity while preserving source insertion order and cache publication behavior.
Skip animation-pointer pre-scans when the source parser owns deferred material initialization.
Delete unused native clip/sampler lowerers and exercise the active source-packaging path in the clip tests.
Remove test-only pointer dispatch and texture-owner helpers; use the active function binding and replacement ownership paths in fixtures.
Reuse cppFunction for node-material fixture extraction so C++ function boundaries are independent of checkout line endings.
Reuse contentFingerprint for vcpkg manifest identity instead of duplicating recursive traversal and hashing.
Reuse writeJsonRecord for atomic shipping results and dependency-plan publication.
Compile selected shipping shader directories in one shared pass so compiler identities are computed once.
Allocate shipping compiler jobs from the CPU and memory budget instead of limiting each selected scene to one job.
Place shared dependency-feature selection beside the existing native CMake modules so build stamps already track it.
Let holdDistLock own and propagate its nesting marker instead of assigning it again in shipping orchestration.
